extra.message: Hardcoded Default SECRET_KEY in Configuration — Complete authentication bypass: attackers can forge JWT tokens for any user with any role, gaining full access to the application. [verified: The hardcoded default secret_key is used for JWT HS256 signing in security.py:52/57 with no startup guard forcing override; if the env var is unset in production, attackers who know the default can forge tokens for any user/role.]

Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) in Jinja2 rendering — Remote code execution on the server with the application's privileges, full system compromise. [verified: Line 90 (same as finding 1): unsandboxed Jinja2 Template renders user-supplied 'fragment' directly; SSTI payloads achieve server-side code execution.]

OS Command Injection via unsanitized host parameter — Arbitrary command execution on the host operating system with the application's privileges. [verified: Line 104 (same as finding 0): os.system('ping -c 1 ' + host) with unsanitized user input; shell metacharacters enable arbitrary command execution.]

Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) in /ops/jinja/ticket-cast-378 — Remote code execution via Jinja2 template engine with full access to Python runtime. [verified: Line 90: user-controlled 'fragment' is concatenated into a Jinja2 Template string and rendered unsandboxed; {{config}} or os.popen payloads achieve RCE.]

OS Command Injection in /ops/shell/ticket-probe-398 — Remote code execution on the server with the privileges of the application process. [verified: Line 104: user-controlled query param 'host' is concatenated directly into os.system('ping -c 1 ' + host) with zero sanitization; shell metacharacters enable arbitrary command execution.]

SSRF via admin-configured webhook target URLs — An admin (or attacker who compromises admin credentials) can configure webhooks to exfiltrate data to external servers or probe internal network services. [verified: The WebhookCreate schema (schemas.py line 420-424) only validates that target_url starts with 'http://' or 'https://' with no IP-range or network filtering, and the webhooks service (services/webhooks.py line 52) calls httpx.Client.post(hook.target_url) with no custom transport, proxy, or destination restrictions — an admin (or compromised admin) can configure webhooks targeting internal IPs (127.]

Password reset tokens logged to plaintext file — Account takeover — anyone with filesystem access can read active reset tokens and reset any user's password. [verified: Same vulnerability as finding 0: the plaintext password reset token is appended to storage/emails.log at lines 139-148 with no encryption or access restriction, allowing any filesystem reader to extract usable reset tokens.]

Password Reset Tokens Exposed in Plaintext Log File — Account takeover: an attacker with filesystem access can read password reset tokens from the log and take over any user account. [verified: The password_reset/request endpoint writes the plaintext reset token to storage/emails.log (lines 139-148) — anyone with filesystem access to settings.storage_path can read active tokens and take over any account. No access control or encryption protects the log file.]

Path Traversal — Arbitrary File Write via unsanitized ref parameter — Arbitrary file write to any location the application can access, enabling code execution or data tampering. [verified: Line 55 (same as finding 5): BASE_EXPORT_DIR / f'{ref}.json' with no resolve() guard; '..' traversal writes JSON files to arbitrary locations.]

Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) via unsanitized endpoint parameter — Access to internal network services, cloud metadata endpoints, and potentially local file read on the server. [verified: Line 75 (same as finding 3): urllib.request.urlopen(endpoint) with no allowlist; internal services and cloud metadata endpoints are reachable.]

CORS origin mirror with credentials allows cross-origin data theft — Any malicious website can make authenticated API requests on behalf of logged-in users and exfiltrate responses, potentially accessing all user data. [verified: Lines 83-86 (same as finding 8): mirrored Origin header with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials:true permits credentialed requests from any origin.]

Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) in /ops/relay/ticket-probe-354 — Access internal network services, cloud metadata endpoints (AWS IMDS, GCP metadata), and internal APIs not otherwise reachable. [verified: Line 75: user-controlled 'endpoint' goes directly to urllib.request.urlopen() with no scheme/host validation; internal metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254) are reachable.]

Path Traversal — Arbitrary File Write via unsanitized name parameter — Write arbitrary files anywhere on the server filesystem, enabling code execution, configuration tampering, or data destruction. [verified: Line 96 (same as finding 6): BASE_EXPORT_DIR / name with no path traversal check; '../..' sequences write arbitrary files anywhere.]

CORS Origin Reflection with Credentials in /ops/origin/ticket-mirror-368 — Arbitrary origins can make authenticated cross-origin requests, potentially stealing sensitive data from authenticated sessions. [verified: Lines 83-86: Origin header is echoed in Access-Control-Allow-Origin alongside Access-Control-Allow-Credentials:true; any origin can make credentialed cross-origin requests.]

NoSQL Injection via unsanitized MongoDB filter — Bypass of query logic, potential data exfiltration from MongoDB, and possible server-side JavaScript execution. [verified: Line 119 (same as finding 2): MongoDB find_one(query) with unsanitized user filter; $where and operator injection bypass intended query logic.]

Path Traversal (Arbitrary File Write) in /ops/dock/ticket-shelf-387 — Arbitrary file write on the server filesystem, potentially overwriting critical files or planting malicious content. [verified: Line 96: user-controlled 'name' builds path BASE_EXPORT_DIR / name with no traversal guard; arbitrary binary content can be written anywhere on the filesystem.]

NoSQL Injection in /ops/mongo/ticket-lane-418 — Bypass intended MongoDB query logic; potentially read arbitrary collections or execute server-side JavaScript via $where. [verified: Line 119: user-supplied JSON filter is passed directly to MongoDB find_one() with no sanitization; $ne/$gt/$where operators bypass query logic or enable JS execution.]

Session Cookies Not Marked Secure by Default — Session cookies transmitted over unencrypted HTTP can be intercepted by network attackers, enabling session hijacking. [verified: cookie_secure defaults to False in config.py:31 and is passed to Response.set_cookie in auth.py:41, so session cookies lack the Secure flag by default, enabling MITM interception on non-HTTPS connections.]

Session cookie missing Secure flag by default — Session hijacking via network sniffing on non-HTTPS connections — an attacker can steal the JWT session token and impersonate the user. [verified: Same issue as finding [1] — cookie_secure defaults to False in config.py:31 and is used in auth.py:41, so session cookies omit the Secure flag by default.]

Missing Rate Limiting on Authentication Endpoints — Brute-force password guessing, credential stuffing attacks, and denial of service via excessive auth requests. [verified: No rate-limiting middleware, decorator, or library (slowapi, etc.) exists anywhere in the codebase; the login, register, and password-reset endpoints are publicly reachable with unlimited request frequency, enabling brute-force and credential-stuffing attacks.]

Missing rate limiting on authentication endpoints — Brute-force password guessing attacks and denial of service against authentication services, leading to account compromise. [verified: Identical to finding 1: no rate-limiting mechanism (slowapi, custom middleware, or decorator) is present on any auth endpoint, leaving login, register, and password-reset fully exposed to unlimited automated requests.]

CSV Formula Injection in SLA Report CSV Export — When an admin opens the exported SLA CSV in a spreadsheet application, attacker-controlled ticket subjects can execute arbitrary formulas/commands, potentially leading to code execution on the admin's machine. [verified: Ticket subject (t.subject) is user-controlled, stored without formula-injection sanitization, then written via csv.writer on line 133-134 with no prefix escaping or =/+/-/@ stripping. No CSV formula sanitization utility exists anywhere in the codebase.]

CSV Formula Injection in Escalations CSV Export — When an admin opens the exported escalations CSV in a spreadsheet application, attacker-controlled escalation reasons can execute arbitrary formulas/commands, potentially leading to code execution on the admin's machine. [verified: Escalation reason (e.reason) is user-controlled text stored as-is, then written via csv.writer on line 186 with no formula-character sanitization. No sanitization exists anywhere in the codebase; csv.writer only handles delimiter quoting, not formula injection.]

Missing CSRF Protection on State-Changing Endpoints — Cross-site request forgery attacks could perform state-changing actions (create tickets, change status, add replies, etc.) on behalf of authenticated users. [verified: No CSRF tokens, middleware, or double-submit cookie pattern exists anywhere in the codebase on any POST/PATCH/DELETE endpoint; SameSite=Lax alone is not a complete CSRF defense per OWASP and leaves gaps for browsers without SameSite support and certain top-level navigation attacks.]

CSV Formula Injection in ticket and report exports — When exported CSV files are opened in spreadsheet applications, embedded formulas can execute commands or exfiltrate data from the user's machine. [verified: Same vulnerability as finding 0: user-controlled ticket subjects with no formula-character validation flow directly into CSV export cells in export_tickets_csv, sla_export_csv, and escalations_export_csv without any prepended quote or formula-trigger stripping.]

CSV Formula Injection in Multiple Export Endpoints — When exported CSV is opened in spreadsheet software, arbitrary commands or data exfiltration can occur via embedded formulas. [verified: Ticket subjects from user input (min_length=3 only, no formula-char filter) are written directly to CSV cells at tickets.py:249, reports.py sla_export_csv, and reports.py escalations_export_csv with no prepended single-quote or stripping of =+@- characters; no compensating control exists.]

SSRF via Admin-Configured Webhook Target URLs — An attacker with admin access can probe internal network services, cloud metadata endpoints, and internal APIs by configuring webhooks with internal target URLs. [verified: target_url is validated only for http/https scheme in WebhookCreate (schemas.py:417–420); no IP-blocklist, host allowlisting, or DNS-resolution guard exists before the URL reaches httpx.Client.post() in deliver_event (webhooks.py:54). Admin auth is required but the threat model explicitly treats admin-compromise SSRF as in-scope.]

Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in /ops/copy/ticket-copy-badge-028 — Execution of arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's browser, enabling session theft, credential phishing, or data exfiltration. [verified: Line 24: user-controlled 'copyline' is concatenated into an HTML string returned as HTMLResponse with no HTML encoding; <script> tags execute in the browser.]

Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in copy endpoint — Execution of arbitrary JavaScript in a victim's browser, potentially stealing cookies, session tokens, or performing actions on the victim's behalf. [verified: Line 24 (same as finding 7): unencoded user input concatenated into HTMLResponse; script injection executes in the victim's browser.]

Open Redirect via unsanitized lane parameter — Phishing attacks — users can be redirected to attacker-controlled sites that mimic the legitimate application to steal credentials. [verified: Line 42 (same as finding 10): RedirectResponse(lane) with no URL validation; attackers redirect users to external phishing sites.]

Denial of Service via Unbounded Count Parameter in /ops/spool/ticket-fan-307 — An attacker can trigger memory exhaustion and crash the application by supplying an extremely large count value (e.g., 100 million), causing denial of service. [verified: The count query parameter has no upper-bound validation, and range(count) with an attacker-supplied huge value (e.g., 100,000,000) materializes that many dicts in memory, exhausting server resources and causing denial of service.]

Weak PRNG used for security-sensitive code generation — Generated codes are predictable, allowing an attacker to guess tokens, bypass authorization checks, or predict future values. [verified: Line 111 (same as finding 12): random.choice() for code generation is predictable; Mersenne Twister state recovery enables token guessing.]

SSL certificate verification disabled for outbound HTTPS requests — Man-in-the-middle attacks on outbound HTTPS connections, allowing interception and modification of supposedly secure traffic. [verified: Line 126 (same as finding 4): ssl._create_unverified_context() disables certificate verification; MITM interception of outbound HTTPS traffic is possible.]

Use of Predictable PRNG for Code Generation in /ops/nonce/ticket-roll-408 — Predictable code generation could allow an attacker to guess or predict generated codes/tokens. [verified: Line 111: random.choice() (Mersenne Twister) is used instead of secrets module for code generation; PRNG state can be predicted after observing sufficient outputs.]

Disabled TLS Certificate Verification in /ops/trust/ticket-drift-428 — Man-in-the-middle attacks possible on outbound HTTPS connections; sensitive data could be intercepted. [verified: Line 126: ssl._create_unverified_context() disables TLS certificate verification on the outbound request; MITM attacks are possible against the fetched endpoint.]

Hardcoded Database Credentials in Default Configuration — Unauthorized database access if default credentials are not overridden in production. [verified: Default database_url in config.py:24 embeds hardcoded credentials support_desk:support_desk@localhost; the localhost host limits remote exploitation unless the DB is separately exposed to the network.]

Account enumeration via login and registration responses — An attacker can enumerate valid user accounts by analyzing differing server responses, then target those accounts with credential stuffing or phishing attacks. [verified: Login returns 401 for invalid credentials but 403 for a disabled account with valid credentials, leaking disabled-account existence; registration returns 409 (not 201) for an existing email despite the generic message, leaking registered-email enumeration via status code.]

Sensitive Bearer token logged in application logs — Session token exposure — JWT tokens in logs allow anyone with log access to impersonate users. [verified: Line 48 (same as finding 9): Authorization header logged in plaintext; JWT tokens captured in logs allow session impersonation.]

Log Injection via Raw Request Body in /ops/wire/ticket-tally-210 — Log forgery (injecting fake log entries), log pollution, and potential exposure of sensitive Authorization headers in logs. [verified: Line 48: raw request body and Authorization header are logged at WARNING level; sensitive Bearer tokens are written to plaintext logs accessible to ops staff.]

MD5 Hash Usage in /ops/digest/ticket-fold-272 — MD5 is susceptible to collision attacks; no direct exploit path in this demo endpoint but indicates poor cryptographic practices. [verified: Lines 65-68: hashlib.md5() is used for digesting user input; while no direct exploit path exists in this endpoint, MD5 is cryptographically broken and indicates poor practice.]
